name: Luna 2 (Second Soviet Space Rocket)

location.name: Near Autolycus crater, between Mare Imbrium and Mare Serenitatis (approximate)

headline: The first human-made object to reach another world
story: On 13 September 1959, a Soviet probe carrying metal emblems struck the Moon at just over three kilometres per second. Launched a day and a half earlier, the Second Soviet Space Rocket, later called Luna 2, became the first object of human origin to touch another celestial body. Its spent upper stage followed about thirty minutes later.

On the way down, its instruments made the first measurements of physical fields around another world. The magnetometer found no significant lunar magnetic field, and the radiation detectors found no hint of a radiation belt.

Its exact impact point has never been identified. NASA's catalogue places the impact only roughly, near 30 degrees north on the plains by Autolycus crater. Whatever is left of it, emblems included, lies somewhere on those plains.

images.caption: Apollo 15's mapping camera looks north across the region in 1971: Autolycus in the centre, Aristillus beyond it, the Marsh of Decay at lower left. Luna 2 came down somewhere on these plains twelve years earlier.
